findings.summary: The whole 30-file / 6,257-line palette component layer has ZERO automated coverage — no guard imports it, no rule scopes it, and a total render failure leaves every guard green.
findings.verification: Structural: for each of the 16 tsx invocations chained into `npm run test:palette`, read its import list — every one resolves into palette/core/**, palette/features/**, store/**, utils/** or gradient-explorer/**; not one imports palette/components/**. `grep -rln 'PickerWall|FavientsPanel|ChannelGraphEditor|GeneratorStage|ImageStage|CanonicalHero|StopsDockPanel|SelectionOverlay|GradientSourcePicker' debug/ .claude/rules/` returns EMPTY. Empirical falsification: changed GradientStrip.tsx's paint guard from `ramp.length !== 256` to `!== 255`, which makes the canvas routine return early always, so EVERY gradient strip in the suite (Generator A/B sources, result hero, Favients previews, Picker hero) renders blank. `npm run test:palette` exit 0; `npm run typecheck` exit 0. Reverted with a targeted Edit; `git diff --stat` clean afterwards.
findings.rationale:
CLAIM: the component layer is unguarded, and the guard named for this subsystem cannot detect even a total rendering failure in it. EVIDENCE: above — structural and empirical. This is NOT a criticism of test:palette, which is healthy and does exactly what it claims: it covers the DOM-free core math (stopFit, channelCurve, facets, easings, generatorPipeline, img2grad, selectionGeometry, wallLayout, rampGeometry, editorConfig). The gap is that nothing was written for the layer above it, and the name `test:palette` implies otherwise — the run's 'healthy but cited for the wrong thing' mode, compounded by plain absence.

CONSEQUENCE, concretely. PickerWall.tsx (1077 lines) holds the column-major index math, the chunk split at MAX_CANVAS_CSS_H, the zoom/pan transform and the lasso/rect/paint carve commit. FavientsPanel.tsx (1147) holds the drop-index computation against the VISIBLE list (dragged item spliced out), the new-group split on the empty tail's lower half, and the trash zone. ChannelGraphEditor.tsx (811) holds the rampToTrack/trackToRamp driver and the CURVE_FRAMES<->256-sample mapping. All pure, all trivially testable, all unguarded. A regression in any of them is invisible to CI and reaches production, which auto-deploys from main.

OPTIONS:
(a) Extract PickerWall's pure index math (k->(col,row), its inverse, and the chunk split) into palette/core/wallLayout.ts and assert it in debug/test-palette-walllayout.mts. Both already exist; that guard currently asserts only shouldSquare/squareCols/STRIP_ROWS_MAX. Adds assertions, not infrastructure.
(b) Same treatment for FavientsPanel's drop-index computation — extract `dropIndexFor(visibleList, y)` into palette/core/favientDnd.ts (already imported by the panel) and assert reorder / insert / new-group / trash.
(c) A browser smoke booting gradient-explorer.html that asserts a non-blank strip — the only thing that would have caught the GradientStrip break above. The owner does visual testing personally and screenshot smokes are explicitly unwanted, so this must be a PIXEL-VARIANCE assertion (the canvas is not uniform), never a baseline image.
(d) Do nothing to the code; just record the gap in a palette rule so a green test:palette is not misread as component coverage.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) then (b). Both are pure-function extractions into modules that already have guards, and they cover the two highest-risk index computations in the subsystem. Do (d) regardless — it costs nothing and prevents the exact misreading that produced this finding. (c) only if a blank-render regression actually ships. NOT APPLIED: new guards are unreviewed code, and refactoring PickerWall/FavientsPanel to extract functions is a real code change with no guard to catch a mistake — precisely the situation the tiering exists for.

findings.summary: Header said each chunk canvas is "drawn ONCE" and never mentioned virtualization; the code deliberately unmounts and repaints chunks on scroll, zoom and selection.
findings.change: Replaced the render-model bullet with the actual model: IntersectionObserver-virtualized chunks, the three repaint triggers, and the half of the old claim that still holds (no per-frame redraw, no repaint on plain DOM scroll). Flags the paint effect as a hot path.
findings.verification: The paint effect returns early on !visible, and `visible` is driven by an IntersectionObserver with rootMargin 500px whose own comment says "Toggling (not latching) is what keeps zooming cheap — otherwise every chunk ever seen stays mounted and redraws on each zoom step" — i.e. the code documents repainting while the header denies it. Three triggers confirmed from the dep array [visible, entries, sprite, cols, nrows, cellW, cellH, swatchW, swatchH, cssW, cssH, selectedId]: viewport re-entry (visible), zoom commit (grep ewWStart — zoom multiplies swatchW and the scaled value is passed down through GroupRow to the chunk), and selection change (selectedId, because the selected swatch is redrawn enlarged in place).

So step 1 of the protocol (invariant verification) had nothing to check here and nothing to downgrade — the drift instead lives in prose headers, which is why every finding this cycle is a header claim. Worth knowing for the tree-wide @invariant sweep: palette/components contributes zero to the 152-file count, and the ten corrections below would all have been @invariant-shaped claims had anyone written them as annotations.

COMMIT MIS-ATTRIBUTION — A NEW FAILURE MODE, NOT THE ONE PROTOCOL.MD RECORDS. My ChannelGraphEditor.tsx change is committed inside a2f1ec49, whose subject is 'audit(p01a-palette-core): importFormats' @invariant carried no proof clause'. I did NOT stage broadly — I ran `git add palette/components/ChannelGraphEditor.tsx` for exactly one path, as required. The cause is different: parallel auditors share one working tree AND therefore one git INDEX. The p01a auditor already had palette/core/importFormats.ts staged; my add joined it in the same index; their `git commit` then took both. The pre-commit hook even announced it — 'typechecking (2 staged TS file(s))' — and my own commit returned exit 1 with 'no changes added to commit'. PROTOCOL.md's fix (stage explicit paths) does not prevent this and cannot: `git add` + `git commit` is not atomic across processes. Real fixes, for the orchestrator: (a) give each auditor its own worktree (`git worktree add`), which gives it its own index — the clean answer; (b) failing that, have auditors verify `git log -1 --name-only` lists exactly their paths after every commit and report when it does not. I adopted (b) for the rest of the session; no later commit was affected. Content landed intact and I verified it after the fact. History was NOT rewritten — rebasing a shared branch under two live auditors is far more dangerous than a wrong subject line.

SEAM HANDOFFS.
(1) TO p01a — palette/core/presetCatalog.ts's top-of-file JSDoc says '24 GRADIENT_PRESETS'; the real length is 25 (verified by importing data/gradientPresets.ts). I fixed the identical stale count in my GradientSourcePicker.tsx but did not touch theirs.

(3) The FavientsPanel/CanonicalHero/HeroSlot staleness is ONE cluster from ONE commit pair — c9da3793 (2026-06-09) removed starring, 3ceb5592 (2026-06-14) brought it back, and three files still describe the world between those dates. (5) Also verified accurate and left alone: PickerWall's column-major formula (code matches k -> col=floor(k/nrows), row=k%nrows exactly), its 3x/2x hover-zoom factors, MAX_CANVAS_CSS_H=2200, SelectionOverlay's pointer-events:none, ChannelGraphEditor's CURVE_FRAMES/256-sample mapping, HeroSlot's railOnly documentation, and all ten componentRegistry ids (panel-favients, palette-generator-extras, palette-modifier-actions, palette-modify-toggles, palette-noise-targets, palette-image-extras, palette-editor-dock, palette-quality-pad, palette-theme-chips, palette-bundle-toggles) — every one resolves to a real registration.

PROPOSED palette RULE — COMPONENT-LAYER SECTION (I did NOT create .claude/rules/palette.md; all three auditors would have collided writing it). Whoever writes it should include: (i) GUARDS — `npm run test:palette` is 16 chained tsx scripts and covers palette/core/** ONLY; it reaches no file under palette/components/**, proven by falsification (blanking GradientStrip left it green). State that plainly so a green run is never read as component coverage. Note also that check:rule-guards resolves a chained npm script by its FIRST command only, so citing test:palette from a rule only ever resolves debug/test-palette-stopfit.mts — cite the specific link you mean. (ii) THE ARCHITECTURE CARVE-OUT — palette/components/** are store-aware composed panels by design and are NOT under the components/ui/** purity rule; do not 'fix' a store import here. The boundary that IS real: palette/ may import engine and shared code freely but must never import app-gmt/, fluid-toy/ or gradient-explorer/ (currently 0 violations — a cheap grep to keep green). (iii) HOST-AGNOSTICISM — components reach hosts only through registries and seams: componentRegistry ids, store/sendTargetRegistry, palette/core/favientTargets' capability flags (select-mode / browse / studio), and the gradientEditorEntrance seam. A component must not branch on which app it is in. (iv) UNDO — palette gestures ride the ENGINE param undo stack via palette/store/paramUndoBracket (aliased as genEdit/editorEdit/favEdit); discrete gestures self-bracket, drags open on pointerdown and close on window pointerup. Snapshots come from registered history providers (captureGeneratorHistory, captureFavientsHistory) in registerPaletteUI. (v) ANNOTATIONS — this directory has zero @invariant/@assumption markers today; new load-bearing claims should be written as annotations with a named proof command, not as prose in the header, which is exactly how the ten drifts fixed this cycle became invisible.
